# Hypersquare Geometry {#sec-hypersquares}

Having established the classical framework in @sec-polytopes, we now consider a modification in which the ambient space is no longer assumed to carry a Riemannian metric. A *hypersquare* will refer, informally, to an $n$-cube equipped with a combinatorial structure that replaces the usual smooth notions of distance and curvature.

::: {#def-hypersquare}
#### Hypersquare
[@exm-unit-cube @def-face]{.uses}
An $n$-dimensional *hypersquare* consists of a combinatorial $n$-cube $Q$ together with:

1. An assignment of a transport operator $T_e$ to each oriented edge $e$ of $Q$, and  
2. A coherence condition on each 2-face requiring that the composition of transport operators around the boundary of the face is equal to a fixed face-dependent automorphism.
:::

We write $\Hsq{n}$ for an $n$-dimensional hypersquare. Instead of a metric tensor, we therefore work with these discrete transport operators and their associated coherence data.

::: {#exm-trivial-hypersquare}
#### The trivial hypersquare
[@def-hypersquare]{.uses}
Assigning the identity to every oriented edge and to every 2-face gives a hypersquare: every composition around a face is the identity.
:::

:::: {.block-tip}
::: {.block-header}
A note on notation
:::
The macro `\Hsq` is defined in this course's own `macros.tex`, at the root of the project; macros like `\Rb` come with the mathkit extension. Blocks like this one (`block-tip`, `block-info`, `block-warning`, …) look the same on the web and in the PDF.
::::

::: {#rem-no-differentiability}
This setup allows us to speak of parallel transport and holonomy without requiring differentiability!
:::

Every 2-face imposes one coherence condition, so @prp-cube-faces counts them for us.

::: {#cor-coherence-count}
[@def-hypersquare @prp-cube-faces]{.uses}
A hypersquare $\Hsq{n}$ satisfies exactly $\binom{n}{2} 2^{n-2}$ coherence conditions.
:::

::: {.proof .smile}
Apply @prp-cube-faces with $k = 2$. (On the website this proof ends with a smile instead of a square: it is written using `::: {.proof .smile}`.)
:::

::: {.block-warning}
::: {.block-header}
Coherence is not commutativity
:::
The condition on a 2-face fixes the composition *around* the face, not the order of the individual transports. Two transport operators along adjacent edges need not commute.
:::

## Fundamental Phenomena {#sec-hypersquares-fundamental-phenomena}

One immediate consequence of this weakened structure is that standard metric identities hold only locally, if at all. For example, while @thm-pythagoras continues to describe distances within individual faces that admit Euclidean charts, there is no guarantee that these local computations are compatible when extended across the entire hypersquare. As a result, geodesic paths---defined here as sequences of edges minimizing a suitable discrete action---need not be unique, and may exhibit periodicity or self-intersection without degeneracy. These phenomena will form the basis for later constructions, where hypersquares serve as model spaces for more general non-metric topological objects.

::: {#cnj-local-pythagoras}
#### Local Pythagoras
[@def-hypersquare @thm-pythagoras]{.uses}
If every 2-face of $\Hsq{n}$ admits a Euclidean chart, then @thm-pythagoras holds along every geodesic of $\Hsq{n}$.
:::
